note: balanceConfig — every number of MANO SURVIVOR in one place: difficulty per chapter, the chapter timeline, enemies, drops, rewards, chests, grades, fusion, coin stats and in-run upgrades. Starting values for experiments, tuned with bots (scripts/survivor-balance.mjs, survivor-campaign.mjs); not measured with people.

logicalArena.note: the mobile game's field (360 × 640 screen, portrait): balls bounce and Mano stops at bounds; the PC game has its own (logicalArenaPc)

logicalArenaPc.note: the PC game's field: larger than its screen (1152 × 648 logical, ui.json → pc), about 1.45× its play area each way; the camera follows Mano over it. view: the screen's play area (1152 × 648 minus ui.json → pc.inset): monsters come in inside it and then keep to the whole field (those Mano walks away from stay behind, out of sight); the balls bounce off the field's edges (they fly on past the screen as the monsters stand there; the friend cats and a class's units go after monsters anywhere on the field within their leash of Mano), as on the phone, where the field is the screen. Mano walks the whole field. spawnBox: monsters come in on the edge of this box around Mano (inside the view) — the phone field's area, so they come as near and as thick as on the phone though the PC screen holds about 3.4× as much; see scripts/survivor-platform-parity.mjs. speedMul: Mano runs this much faster than on the phone (asked for: on the wide PC field she felt slow).

xp.note: next = round(previous × growth + add). Experience left lying flies to Mano by itself after pullAfter seconds

overtime.note: the chapter is cleared only when the boss falls. Past 240 s with the boss alive the fight goes on (boss overtime): every 30 s monsters come 15% faster; and monsters (and the boss) hit hitsHarder× harder every 30 s, so a run that can no longer win ends

mobSpeed.note: and the ordinary monsters run faster the longer the chapter's boss lives: from `after` s after it came, ×(1 + step) more every `every` s, never past ×max (a step of the clock, not of each frame); back to ×1 the moment it falls, and every run starts at ×1. Elites and bosses keep their own speed

chapter.packNote: each spawn is a pack: `pack` monsters of one kind together at one point of the edge, every `spawnInterval` s (fewer if the screen is near enemySoftLimit). Monster HP climbs steeply through the chapter (hpMultiplier) because Mano's in-run upgrades multiply. The first 70 s bring 1.5× then 1.3× the monsters they used to (the opening was too empty), each with less HP (about the same HP a second as before, so a single-target build such as the friend cats keeps up) and worth a little less experience (xpMultiplier, ordinary monsters only; 1 when missing, so Mano levels about as fast as before). More than that (2.4× / 1.6×) piled up faster than a new player's one ball kills and ended chapter 1 for a player standing still in under 30 s. Bots: clear rates about as before on chapters 1-8 (phone and PC, good and casual players) and 10/15 (ball and cat builds)

beyondLastChapter.note: each chapter past the list multiplies the last one by these

rewards.note: every coin of chapter N (rewards, coins on the field, coins in its chests) is worth coinGrowth^(N−1), times the coin stat — the same pace as the monsters' HP past chapter 5. First clear with both elites = 8 chests, a repeat clear = 6

chest.note: only weapons that can really be played are rolled (today: the bouncy ball, one roll per chest plus coins)

fusion.note: three of the same weapon and grade make one of the next grade; EX cannot be fused

crit.name: 치명타 확률
crit.note: 0.75% a level, price ×priceGrowth, up to 50% at level 67 (as it always was); past that 1.5% a level, price ×1.05, up to 100% at level 101 (asked for: 100% reachable). At 100% the crit card never comes in a run (game.js).

perma.note: each stat has its own level L (from 0): value × mul^L (or + add × L); next price = floor(price × priceGrowth^L); past: from that level on another step (perma.js). Caps here are game rules for permanent stats, shown in the shop.

split.note: 쪼개지는 행운: out of the pool (taken out at the player's wish); kept so its numbers still read

upgrades.note: in-run only, reset after every run; no cap and no hidden slow-down. The core four: balls per volley ×2, gap between volleys ×0.7, damage ×1.5, bounce limit ×2

catSwap.note: in a run with the cats, the magnet card's place in the pool goes to 냥냥 연금술 (same number of cards, same equal chance); it leaves the pool at its last level

upgrades.catCards: friendCats' cards (friends.js): in runs with the cats all five join the pool (same equal chance as every card); 뚱냥이, 스피드냥이, 빠르게 할퀴기 and 발톱 갈기 only once there is a cat. They change the cats only; the ball's cards change the ball only. 친구냥이 +1 cat; 뚱냥이 size ×mul, hit area ×rangeMul; 스피드냥이 speed ×mul; 빠르게 할퀴기 gap ×mul; 발톱 갈기 damage ×mul.

performance.ballBudgetNote: at most this many balls fly at once; a volley that would pass it fires fewer balls, each carrying the damage of those it stands for (the total never drops)

cats.note: Cat companions (단추·호두·모루). They join for good with chapter 5's first clear (story.json → rewards.forest, with one S-grade red ball and the rerolls, once) and come along from activeFromChapter on. They gather coins and experience lying on the field (each its own pick, all three on different ones; everything within `magnet` of a cat flies to it, so a pile goes in one sweep), never fight, never get hurt and never block Mano. Hearts they only take with 냥냥 연금술. The fighting cats are another thing: friendCats.

rerolls.note: redraws of the upgrade cards (chapter 5's reward opens them: story.json → rewards.forest.rerolls a run). From fromChapter on every run starts with that many; a redraw puts the three cards on show back and draws three others the same way (equal chances; other than those shown while the pool has enough).

friendCats.note: 친구냥이 (friends.js): fighting cats in runs with the cats. Each 친구냥이 card brings one more (+1). One scratch = catBase × 발톱 갈기, where catBase = the ball's damage at the start of the run (base × grade × coin stat 공격 피해) × damageCoef; Mano's 치명타 확률 and 치명타 피해 apply. The gap between scratches = interval × the coin stat 공격 주기 × 빠르게 할퀴기. The scratch hits every monster in a circle of radius swipe at reach in front of the cat (뚱냥이 grows both, and the cat's size up to maxDrawScale as drawn). speed: px/s; leash: how far from Mano a cat goes after monsters (on screen only); seekEvery: s between looks for a better target; aim: how a cat chooses (friends.js, in seconds of 'how soon it could strike'): edge — how much of a monster's size counts in the run to it (0: from its middle, so a big one does not draw every cat), near — the run to it counted again × near (the nearer of two wins while the claw comes back), covered — later a monster counts whose HP the other cats' booked scratches already cover (a boss's never is), coming — later (softer) one the cats still on their way to it would finish, crowd — later for each other cat about to strike it, clump — earlier for each other monster inside a scratch's circle of it (up to clumpMax), switchMargin — how much better another must be before a cat changes targets; attackSeconds: the scratch's length (shorter, down to minAttackSeconds, when the gap is shorter), strikeAt: its share where the claw lands; recoverSeconds: the paw coming back (drawn); firstScratch: the most a new cat waits; homeRadius: where cats wait near Mano with nothing to fight; powerAt: 발톱 갈기's multiplier from which the scratch is drawn golden; packBonus: every cat beyond the first adds this to every cat's scratch (1 + packBonus × (cats − 1)); drawH: an idle cat's height in field px.

percentHeart.note: a 퍼센트 하트 heals this share of the maximum HP (set per 냥냥 연금술 level). Only cats make them, from a normal heart; they are never turned again and only Mano picks them up.

lateGame.note: From fromChapter on, each phase of the chapter (same order as chapter.phases) multiplies the monsters' HP and their hits on top of everything else, so the middle and the end of a run stay a fight; elites and the boss get specialHp, each its own (the thief comes early, at 70 s, and must be catchable in its 30 s, so it gets no extra). It comes in step by step: a little at fromChapter, all of it from fullAtChapter on. Chapters before fromChapter are untouched.

writer.note: From Tizzzz's chapter on (she rewrites a card at every level-up, so a run's build ends far stronger than before), each phase of the run multiplies the monsters' HP and hits once more, on top of the push above; mid-boss and boss get specialHp (the thief none, so it stays catchable). Tuned so a bot that takes her edits clears chapter 21 a little less often than it did before she came.

bossGuard.note: From fromChapter on (with Tizzzz: she joins at chapter 15's clear) the skull king loses at most maxShare of its HP each second (burst: seconds' worth that can go at once; damage over that is lost) and hits `hits`× harder (body, charge, slam). With 0.04 a fight lasts at least 25 s however strong the build, and the king can still hurt it. Tuned on bots that pick like a person (the 'human' policy).

tizzzz.note: The writer Tizzzz joins for good with the reward of chapter 10's first clear (story.json → rewards.deepforest, which also gives an SS red ball and 2 more rerolls). From activeFromChapter on, at every level-up she rewrites one of the cards shown at random (however many are shown; one card, never two): that card does its own effect `times` times over (×2 → ×4, ×1.5 → ×2.25, +8%p → +16%p…), exactly as if it had been chosen that many times, and only if it is chosen. A redraw (reroll) draws new cards and she rewrites one of those afresh. A card that cannot take it (a card with levels too close to its last) is never picked; if none can, the cards are left alone. penSeconds: the pen's pass over the card (the card works from the first moment).

blessings.note: Battle blessings from the story (story.json → rewards). Temporary balance values. chance: per ball hit; perSecond: at most this many of that blessing in one second however many balls fly (a token bucket, so a screen of balls cannot set it off hundreds of times); seconds: how long it lasts on a monster, a new one only renews it (never stacks). The boss is never frozen: the snow blessing slows it instead. Lightning hits are never a ball hit, so they can never set off more lightning (no chains of chains). final (마왕의 탱탱볼) multiplies every chance.

bossTypes.note: the ordinary bosses (the 145 s mid-boss and the 210 s boss of every chapter; the extra special bosses that come after the boss in some chapters fight their own way: extraBosses): each gets ONE of these when it comes, from a shuffled bag of the four (the next four come in a new shuffle), and keeps it until it falls. A: walks, stops, shows the path and charges along it (its own windup, charge speed and charge hit). B: walks at Mano weaving left and right (weave: the most it turns off her direction, radians; period: s for one weave). C: walks, stops, shows three lanes for aim s, then shoots three shots along them (a fan of spread degrees; each hits like its charge). D: walks; then, shown for warn s (it shakes, a ring round it), runs at mul x its speed for seconds s, turning at most turn rad/s, then walks again. Its HP, hits, reward and when it comes do not change. Between its own moves it also uses skills (bossSkills).

bossSkills.note: the ordinary bosses' skills (bosses.js → bossSkills, bossSkill; game.js): besides its own way of fighting (bossTypes A B C D), an ordinary boss uses skills, one after each of its own moves, by turns. Which: byType[its way], the first count[its kind][tier] of them (tier: the chapter's episode, 0 for chapters 1–5 … 6 for 31–35; brute is the 145 s mid-boss). Each skill is an attack of bosses.js (type) with its numbers at tier 0; per: added a tier; warn: less warnPerTier a tier, never under minWarn; speed: ×(1 + speedPerTier × tier); hit: its blows × the boss's own chargeDamage (a body-wide width: 'body'). Under enrage.below of its HP (from enrage.fromTier, the mid-boss from enrage.bruteFromTier) it is enraged: it walks enrage.walk × as long and its skills come two at a time (a combo, enrage.after s apart).

extraBosses.note: The extra special bosses (MANO_EXTRA_BOSSES; bosses.js): in the chapters listed, after the chapter's own boss has fallen, one more boss comes, and the chapter is cleared only when it falls too. The field is cleared first (the monsters fade, their attacks go), then intro: calm s of quiet, warn s of WARNING! with a siren and its name and line, appear s of it coming in (Mano cannot be hurt and it cannot be hit until it stands); its fight is in the play area as it was then (box: the PC camera holds still). hpMul: its HP is the chapter boss's (its chapter and late-game strength) × this (18, from 15 for a longer fight with more of its phases; 15 was six times the 2.5 it had, which was still too quick a fight; it was 0.8 before that), never capped; from lateGame.bossGuard.fromChapter on it has the boss's guard too (it loses at most maxShare of its HP a second), so it is never easier than the boss it follows. damage: each blow's base, × the boss's hit strength. Attacks (each warned from the start in its real shape, the safe ground shown, blows landing once): ringwave (rings out of it across the whole area, gaps of gapDeg° to stand in, one near Mano), bloom (petal fans from it in turn, skip of them left out), spores (big circles over the area in turn), web (beams across the whole area through it, fire of threads), sweep (a band crossing the whole area, gaps of gap px to stand in, push px/s while inside), rows (every other row of the area), branches (fans from it, every other one), pillars (circles along a fan of rays toward Mano), clock (fans from the area's middle in turn round the dial), chess (rows and columns of a board over the area), combo (parts one after another, after s apart), volley (fans of `shots` shots at Mano, `bursts` of them `step` s apart, each aimed where she is when its thin lanes show, laneWarn s before), spiral (`arms` streams of shots wheeling out of it, one each `every` s for `seconds`, turning spin rad/s; twin: a second wheel the other way), dash (it charges straight through where Mano is to the area's edge: the lane warned, the blow along it as it runs, `count` times from where each ends), rain (circles over the area in quick turns: where Mano is, where she is heading, then spread), cross (a + then an × through where she is, across the whole area, `count` in turn). Shots are many small blows (about half a blast each); shot: the look of its shots. walk: s between attacks; recover: s after one. nova (rings of shots all round it, `waves` of `count`, each turned half a step), homing (orbs thrown out wide that turn toward Mano at most turn rad/s for seek s), cage (a ring of blows round Mano with `gap` places left open, then its inside after `after` s), stalk (circles that follow her, each where she is and lead s ahead), beam (narrow fans side by side in turn: a beam swinging sweepDeg through her, and back after `back` s). phases (scripts/survivor-extra-bosses.py): every boss's attack lists by the HP share left (above): four phases, its own attack and three more from the start, a fourth and two-part combos below 75%, a fifth below 50%, only three-part combos close together below 25%, walking less each time; harder each episode (asked for twice: much harder, many more patterns); the last boss: five phases, every kind of attack, three-part combos at the end. Tempo (asked for: the patterns were too slow): warnings ×0.65 (never under minWarn 0.8 s), the steps of a pattern ×0.6, ring and band speeds ×1.4 (then ×2 again: the attacks that show their safe gaps in green fly twice as fast, asked for), combos' gaps ×0.65, walk (s between attacks) and recover halved, its walk ×1.5 faster.
extraBosses.blowCapNote: no single blow of an extra boss (its warned shapes or its body) takes more than this share of Mano's full HP (the last boss: its own blowCap), so one mistake is never the end, however strong the chapter's monsters hit

zyo.note: zyo_'s class change (zyo.js; her names and words: zyo.json). From activeFromChapter on, in a run with her (chapter 15's reward), each recipe's two cards picked `need` times each (run.picks: a card Tizzzz rewrote counts its times) put its class card in the draw, at random among the others. zyo_ adds a card of her own beside the three drawn only `offer` of the time (0: never; asked for: her cards come at random, she marks those that came — her recipe's cards, a class card, after the change the growth card). Once a run. The change ends the ball and the fighting cats; base = the ball's damage × count ÷ gap + one cat's scratch × cats ÷ its gap (no crit) is what the class starts from, never under floor: the run's firepower at its start × e^(floor.perLevel × the levels gone by) (a bot's usual build grows about e^0.26 a level; with need 7 at random a build that put its picks into its recipe can be far behind): on one target with all of it there it deals bonus × base a second (× the recipe's own bonus: B and C, whose ×0.7 gaps add far less than A's and D's ×2 counts and claws, would otherwise change into a class many times weaker; bots: with it, runs that changed class clear about as often whichever it was) × the 전투력 card (shown under the class's own name; in the pool with the eight left, about one level-up in three; damage × (damageMul + damageMulPerLevel × the run's levels past damageMulFrom), rate × rateMul each, to the power `pow` (3: it comes about one level-up in three), so the later in the run the more one adds (by the run's level: a class taken late catches up) and the class keeps up with the attack cards it gave up, whose ×2 and ×1.5 multiply on each other ever faster (bots, levels 30–70, the same seeds: the class ahead of the same run without it on one boss and on a crowd); the rate past rateCap turns into damage). Each unit group deals `share` of that, split over its count, one hit each hitGap (÷ rate). ball: the giant balls that chase (speed px/s, roll: rad/s round their target, radius px); shield (A): giant balls circling Mano at orbit px, spin rad/s, pushing the monsters they touch out by push px, and every monster (not a boss) inside their ring out at pushSpeed px/s; ninja: dash speed, reach px from a target's edge, slashR: the slash's circle round the target; leash: how far from Mano they go (on screen only); the first half of the units (rounded up) go for a boss or an elite anywhere on screen while there is one. revive (B): once a run (times), the blast hits within radius px with `seconds` of the class's one-target damage, a boss at most bossCap of its HP (through a guard), then full HP and inv s safe. lifesteal (C): a monster's whole HP taken heals mob (a boss's, an elite's: boss) × Mano's full HP; never more than perSecond of it a second. warp (D): holes at `at` (shares of the field; the extra boss's area during its fight), radius px; after a warp she must leave the exit hole and cooldown s pass; clear px round the exit cleared of monsters; inv s safe. keep: the cards left after the change (with 전투력). fxSeconds: the notes' moment (she cannot be hurt; the new attack starts after it). skill: every `every` s (÷ the rate, first after `first` s) the class casts over the screen — 탱탱 메테오 or 그림자 분신: count strikes (+1 each perLevels 전투력, up to max) on monsters on screen (a boss or an elite first), each landing delay s later (stagger s apart) and hitting every monster within radius px; together share × the class's one-target damage a second. growth: each 전투력 picked makes the giant balls, the shield balls, the slashes and the skill's circles perLevel bigger (up to maxLevels), never more units.

turret.note: the turret (turret.js; its words: turret.json). From activeFromChapter on, in a run with it (chapter 20's reward), at a level-up turrets can be made beside its card (the card is still chosen; several at once): each takes cost picks of the upgrades this run took (any of them, the same twice or two; never what the class change used of its recipe cards: zyo.need of each, picks past that are material) are taken back exactly and one turret stands at a random spot in the field (margin px in from its edge, apart px from the others, clear px off any monster; the best of tries). One kind only. It shoots the nearest monster within range px every interval s (retry s when none; first s after it is made; kick: its barrel's recoil s): a blow of power × the run's main attack now (before the class change its ball and cats, a second; after it the class's strength at the change × its 전투력 cards, never the dead ball's numbers; never under a usual build's at its level: zyo.js → floor; turret.js → turretBase) × interval — the same for every turret, never more for what was given (taking picks back lowers every turret's blow with the rest). Turrets stay until the run ends; an extra special boss's fight area takes them inside it.
